title: Cross-region metric lag caused silent KEDA underprovision during evening burst
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: On 2026-02-26 at ~19:14 UTC we observed a customer-facing latency and error spike in the hosted inference endpoint cluster serving europe-west and europe-north. The control plane routed traffic normally but pods failed to scale fast enough, causing tail latency >5s for ~18 minutes and visible 5xx errors for a subset of customers. This postmortem documents root cause analysis, short-term mitigations applied during the incident, and action items to prevent recurrence.

What happened: The KEDA external scaler backing the region-sharded worker pool did not trigger a timely scale-up during a sustained burst. The scaler's percentile-based metric (P95 over 5m) was computed by an aggregator that dropped region tags for ~7m due to a recent rollout. Combined with a percentile estimator change in runtime-1.20 that excluded brief microbursts, the scaler computed a value below the configured threshold and did not request replicas. At the same time, HPA scaleDown/stabilization windows were aggressively short (30s) allowing pod churn that reduced warm pool availability and amplified cold-start latency.

Why it matters: This incident shows an interaction between metric aggregation, scaler configuration, and HPA stabilization that caused a false negative (underprovision) at the autoscaling layer. Users experienced degraded latency and errors; internal SLOs were missed for the endpoint for the incident window.
timeline: 2026-02-26 19:10 UTC: Traffic burst begins (customer batch runtimes + promotional traffic).
2026-02-26 19:14 UTC: Monitoring alerts for 99th latency and error-rate fire for eu clusters.
2026-02-26 19:16 UTC: On-call (Liam) acknowledges and starts investigation. Dashboards show pod count steady; KEDA scaler metric below threshold.
2026-02-26 19:18 UTC: Live tail logs show repeated cold starts and queueing at the ingress.
2026-02-26 19:22 UTC: Hotfix applied: temporarily increased HPA minReplicas for affected pool and extended HPA stabilization window to 3m.
2026-02-26 19:30 UTC: Latency begins to recover as additional pods come online from hotfix and warm pool refills.
2026-02-26 19:40 UTC: Incident declared resolved and monitoring kept under watch for 60m.
root_cause: Combination of (1) aggregator rollout that stripped region tags causing KEDA to compute cross-region percentiles incorrectly, (2) percentile estimator change in runtime-1.20 that deweighted short bursts, and (3) aggressive HPA scaleDown/stabilization settings that allowed warm capacity to drop during churn. The net effect was a false negative from the autoscaler during a real sustained burst in one region.
impact_summary: Duration: ~18 minutes of elevated latency with intermittent 5xxs. Affected customers: ~12 high-traffic customers in EU region (estimated 0.4% of active tokens during window). Operational: SLO breach for endpoint 2026-02-26 19:14-19:32 UTC. No data loss or secrets exposure observed.
mitigations: Hotfix 1 (19:22 UTC): Increase minReplicas for eu region worker pool from 4 to 10 to absorb immediate burst.
Hotfix 2 (19:22 UTC): Set HPA stabilization windows to 3m (scaleUp) and 3m (scaleDown) for the affected pools to avoid premature eviction of warm inference pods.
Hotfix 3 (19:30 UTC): Rollback quick aggregator change that removed region tags — restored per-region tag propagation for scaler metrics.
Monitoring: Added immediate dashboard panel to surface region-tagged scaler metrics and KEDA decision_reason logs for live incidents.
action_items: A1: Change KEDA scaling metric for cross-region worker pools from P95 to 'sum' or 'max' across region-tagged buckets where appropriate (owner: Liam, ETA: 2026-03-12).
A2: Revert percentile estimator rollback and add unit tests that include microburst scenarios to ensure estimator does not over-suppress short sustained bursts (owner: Runtime Team, ETA: 2026-03-05).

A3: Increase default HPA stabilization windows in autoscaling-configs for inference pools (scaleUp 2m, scaleDown 4m) and add config guardrails per pool type (owner: Autoscaling Squad, ETA: 2026-03-10).
A4: Implement a KEDA 'decision_reason' audit log tied to the scaler metric sample used for decisions and retain for 7 days (owner: Observability, ETA: 2026-03-20).
A5: Add an end-to-end chaos test that simulates region-local bursts with tag-loss and validates scaling behavior (owner: SRE, ETA: 2026-04-01).
A6: Update runbook for KEDA/HPA incidents to include 'verify region tags on metric path' and 'temporarily raise minReplicas' steps (owner: Oncall Docs, ETA: 2026-03-03).
A7: Schedule a cross-team post-deploy verification step for aggregator rollouts that mutate metric tags (owner: Release Engineering, ETA: 2026-03-08).
follow_up_tasks: Create PR to change metric type and add e2e test for cross-region: github.com/redwood-inference/prs/4589 (owner: Liam)
Runtime team to submit estimator unit test PR: github.com/redwood-inference/prs/4621 (owner: Priya Shah)
Observability to add KEDA decision_reason panel and alert mapping: dashboards.redwood.internal/d/scale-decisions (owner: Marco Rossi)
Postmortem review scheduled in Ops retro on 2026-03-06 (participants: Eng leads, SRE, Product)
Customer outreach draft prepared for affected customers (owner: Customer Success)
